The field is easier to understand when the pieces have a job. Start with a question,
follow the connections, and use a small experiment to make the ideas tangible.

## A map of the field

```{=html}
<div class="field-map"><section class="field-column"><h3>Build a mental model</h3><p>What does the model do, and what surrounds it?</p><ul><li><a href="topics/software-and-data.html" class="">Software and data foundations</a><span>Understand enough of the surrounding software to debug the system when the model is not the problem.</span></li><li><a href="topics/models-and-context.html" class="">Model behavior and context</a><span>Learn what the model sees, what you ask it to do, and how to tell whether a prompt change helped.</span></li><li><a href="topics/openai-interfaces.html" class="">OpenAI interfaces and SDKs</a><span>Choose the interface according to where the application runs and who should own the agent loop.</span></li></ul></section><section class="field-column"><h3>Connect it to the world</h3><p>Where do evidence, tools and control come from?</p><ul><li><a href="topics/retrieval-and-grounding.html" class="">Retrieval and grounding</a><span>Help a model answer from the right evidence, and make that evidence inspectable.</span></li><li><a href="topics/tools-and-mcp.html" class="">Tools and MCP</a><span>Give a model useful capabilities while keeping real permissions and execution under application control.</span></li><li><a href="topics/agents-and-workflows.html" class="">Agents and workflows</a><span>Decide which steps should be fixed in code and which decisions should be delegated to a model.</span></li></ul></section><section class="field-column"><h3>Measure and improve</h3><p>What failed, and which change would help?</p><ul><li><a href="topics/evaluation.html" class="">Evaluation and error analysis</a><span>Turn “it seems good” into a repeatable account of what works, what fails and what changed.</span></li><li><a href="topics/adaptation-and-distillation.html" class="">Training adaptation and distillation</a><span>Understand when changing a model is justified, and how to measure whether the change transfers to unseen tasks.</span></li></ul></section><section class="field-column"><h3>Make it useful</h3><p>How does it become a dependable part of someone’s work?</p><ul><li><a href="topics/multimodal.html" class="">Multimodal and realtime systems</a><span>Choose the interface and timing that fit the task: documents, images, speech, video or interactive audio.</span></li><li><a href="topics/production-and-inference.html" class="">Production and inference</a><span>Make the system reliable, observable and economical under real use.</span></li><li><a href="topics/security.html" class="">Security and trust boundaries</a><span>Keep untrusted model inputs and outputs from becoming unauthorized actions or data access.</span></li><li><a href="topics/product-and-field-engineering.html" class="">Product and field engineering</a><span>Translate a real workflow into a useful system people can understand, evaluate and adopt.</span></li></ul></section></div>
```

::: {.connection-note}
[Evaluation](topics/evaluation.qmd) asks whether a change helped.
[Security](topics/security.qmd) sets boundaries on what the system may do.
[Product engineering](topics/product-and-field-engineering.qmd) defines whose problem it solves.
These concerns run through the whole map.
:::

## Start with a question

```{=html}
<div class="question-grid"><article><h3><a href="investigations/smolagents-and-langgraph.html" class="">How much control should an agent have?</a></h3><p>Understand the tradeoff between a model choosing its next action and a workflow whose transitions are explicit.</p></article><article><h3><a href="questions.html#evaluation" class="">How do I know the system improved?</a></h3><p>Separate a convincing answer from a useful result. Look at failures, supporting evidence and the behavior of the whole system.</p></article><article><h3><a href="questions.html#context" class="">What belongs in the model&#x27;s context?</a></h3><p>Connect instructions, memory, retrieval and tool results to the information the model actually needs.</p></article><article><h3><a href="questions.html#deployment" class="">What makes an experiment useful to someone else?</a></h3><p>Follow the path from a working example to a reliable, understandable part of a person&#x27;s work.</p></article></div>
```

## Find a way into the material

- **Build with OpenAI:** start with the [official quickstart](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/quickstart), then one structured output and one tool.
- **Learn through a project:** [LLM Zoomcamp](https://github.com/DataTalksClub/llm-zoomcamp) connects retrieval, evaluation and deployment.
- **Understand agent context:** the [Hugging Face Context Course](https://huggingface.co/learn/context-course/unit0/introduction) covers skills, MCP, plugins and execution hooks.
- **Understand models:** [Karpathy’s Zero to Hero](https://karpathy.ai/zero-to-hero.html) and the [Hugging Face LLM Course](https://huggingface.co/learn/llm-course/chapter1/1) offer deeper paths.

[Browse courses and lessons](library.html?type=course) or [explore all sources](library.qmd).
